raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation A2 and A3 NPUs do not support FP8 LightningIndexer, so FP16 is the only practical precision for the indexer. This makes the indexer a bottleneck for long-context workloads. This PR adds an int8 quantization option for the NPU LightningIndexer. It stores the indexer key cache as int8 and uses the NPU-native npu_quant_lightning_indexer kernel, delivering a 2× indexer speedup and reducing end-to-end TTFT on Ascend A2/A3. The feature is opt-in via SGLANG_NPU_INDEXER_INT8=True and is disabled by default, preserving existing FP16/FP8 behavior. ## Modifications - python/sglang/srt/environ.py Adds SGLANG_NPU_INDEXER_INT8 = EnvBool(False) as the feature flag for int8 indexer mode. - python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/memory_pool_npu.py Adds indexer_kv_store_int8 and selects index_k_store_dtype = torch.int8 and index_k_scale_dtype = torch.float16 when the flag is enabled. Creates the scale buffer for both FP8 and int8 modes, using index_k_scale_dtype (FP16 for int8, FP32 for FP8). - python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_npu_indexer.py _quantize_npu_indexer_activation now accepts a scale_type argument instead of hardcoding torch.float32 for the scale tensor. forward_npu passes pool.index_k_store_dtype and pool.index_k_scale_dtype into the quantizer. When index_k_store_dtype == torch.int8, the indexer weights are cast to FP16 before calling npu_quant_lightning_indexer, because the int8 kernel requires FP16 weights. ## Accuracy Tests gsm8k shows 93% accuracy for int8 indexer cache LongBenchV2 literary subset tests does not show metric degradations FP16 Indexer INT8 indexer ## Speed Tests and Profiling The int8 lighting indexer itself is 2x faster than fp16 Test by sglang.benchmark.serving python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --gsp-prompts-per-group 17 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix --gsp-system-prompt-len 180000 --gsp-question-len 10828 --gsp-output-len 1 --gsp-num-groups 1 --backend sglang-oai-chat average TTFT reduces from 67402 to 49125 (~-25%) FP16 Indexer INT8 Indexer --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #41488096525](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41488096525) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #41488096135](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41488096135) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #41488096702](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41488096702) > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change. Thanks for this PR. We tested the INT8 indexer's accuracy on GLM-5.2 (A3, tp8) with long
prompts (6k–26k tokens). Short prompts like gsm8k cannot test it: with 2048 tokens or fewer,
the indexer selects every token, so even a broken kernel gives the same answer.

| indexer | copy a long random list | find a value among 650–2100 similar records (15 questions) |
|---|---|---|
| FP16 | 100% | 15 / 15 |
| INT8 (this PR) | 100% | 15 / 15 |
| deliberately broken (control) | 0–19% | 0 / 15 |

In this setup INT8 gives the same results as FP16. We found three other setups that break
when the flag is on. Each inline comment below explains one of them and proposes a fix.
With these fixed, turning the flag on can no longer break DeepSeek-V4, and setups with
prefill CP or an FP8 KV cache keep their current indexer.

Longer term, we would like this to be the default on A2/A3. Before that we plan to check
three more things: the same test at 128k–1M tokens with the usual production launch
flags, one standard long-context benchmark, and no slowdown on short prompts. These three
fixes come first either way.

**Problem.** When the flag is on, `custom_ops` is never imported. Other code needs it:
DeepSeek-V4 on NPU calls `torch.ops.custom.*` ops (`ascend_dsv4_backend.py`, `dsv4_rope.py`,

detail.body: ## Motivation A2 and A3 NPUs do not support FP8 LightningIndexer, so FP16 is the only practical precision for the indexer. This makes the indexer a bottleneck for long-context workloads. Thanks for this PR. We tested the INT8 indexer's accuracy on GLM-5.2 (A3, tp8) with long
prompts (6k–26k tokens). Short prompts like gsm8k cannot test it: with 2048 tokens or fewer,
the indexer selects every token, so even a broken kernel gives the same answer.

| indexer | copy a long random list | find a value among 650–2100 similar records (15 questions) |
|---|---|---|
| FP16 | 100% | 15 / 15 |
| INT8 (this PR) | 100% | 15 / 15 |
| deliberately broken (control) | 0–19% | 0 / 15 |

In this setup INT8 gives the same results as FP16. We found three other setups that break
when the flag is on. Each inline comment below explains one of them and proposes a fix.
With these fixed, turning the flag on can no longer break DeepSeek-V4, and setups with
prefill CP or an FP8 KV cache keep their current indexer.

Longer term, we would like this to be the default on A2/A3. Before that we plan to check
three more things: the same test at 128k–1M tokens with the usual production launch
flags, one standard long-context benchmark, and no slowdown on short prompts. These three
fixes come first either way.
